bio-evo-01-c1.text: The Linnean Society of London (2018). 1st July 2018: 160th anniversary of the presentation of "On the tendency of Species to form Varieties". Linnean Society of London.
bio-evo-01-c1.quote: Unfortunately, neither of the two were present.
bio-evo-01-c1.claim: Lyell and Hooker arranged for both men's papers to be read together at the Linnean Society on 1 July 1858, and neither author attended.

bio-evo-02-c1.text: Bridgett M. vonHoldt, Rebecca Y. Kartzinel, Christian D. Huber, et al (2018). Growth factor gene IGF1 is associated with bill size in the black-bellied seedcracker Pyrenestes ostrinus. Nature Communications.
bio-evo-02-c1.quote: Pyrenestes finches are unique among birds in showing a non-sex-determined polymorphism in bill size and are considered a textbook example of disruptive selection.
bio-evo-02-c1.claim: In African black-bellied seedcracker finches, both large-billed and small-billed individuals outcompete medium-billed birds because there are two distinct seed sizes.

bio-evo-02-c2.text: Stephen J. O’Brien, Warren E. Johnson, Carlos A. Driscoll, et al (2017). Conservation Genetics of the Cheetah: Lessons Learned and New Opportunities. Journal of Heredity.
bio-evo-02-c2.quote: Perhaps the most remarkable indicator of the cheetah’s genetic impoverishment was the demonstration that cheetahs failed to reject surgically implanted skin allografts from unrelated cheetah donors
bio-evo-02-c2.claim: Cheetahs experienced a severe bottleneck ~10,000 years ago and are now so genetically uniform that skin grafts between unrelated cheetahs are not rejected.

bio-evo-03-c1.text: Amal Y. Aldhebiani (2018). Species concept and speciation. Saudi Journal of Biological Sciences.
bio-evo-03-c1.quote: the zoologist Mayr (1942) who defined species as: “groups of actually or potentially interbreeding natural populations which are reproductively isolated from other such groups”
bio-evo-03-c1.claim: The most widely used definition is the biological species concept (Ernst Mayr, 1942): a species is a group of organisms that actually or potentially interbreed and are reproductively isolated from other groups.

bio-evo-04-c2.text: Andrew H. Knoll, Martin A. Nowak (2017). The timetable of evolution. Science Advances.
bio-evo-04-c2.quote: Oxygen concentrations in the atmosphere and surface oceans first rose in the Great Oxygenation Event (GOE) 2.4 billion years ago
bio-evo-04-c2.claim: ~2.4 Ga: Great Oxygenation Event, cyanobacteria flood atmosphere with O2

bio-evo-04-c3.text: Simon Ho (2008). The Molecular Clock and Estimating Species Divergence. Nature Education (Scitable).
bio-evo-04-c3.quote: The molecular clock hypothesis states that DNA and protein sequences evolve at a rate that is relatively constant over time and among different organisms.
bio-evo-04-c3.claim: DNA accumulates mutations at roughly constant rates.

bio-evo-04-c3.text: Jane Gitschier (2010). All About Mitochondrial Eve: An Interview with Rebecca Cann. PLOS Genetics.
bio-evo-04-c3.quote: In a 1987 Nature article, Rebecca Cann and her co-workers, Mark Stoneking and the late Allan Wilson, painstakingly analyzed mitochondrial DNA purified from placentas that had been collected from women of many different ancestral origins.
bio-evo-04-c3.claim: Landmark studies by Cann, Stoneking, and Wilson in 1987 used mtDNA to argue all living humans share a common female ancestor in Africa ~200,000 years ago: 'Mitochondrial Eve'.

bio-evo-05-c1.text: Alexander Fleming (1945). Penicillin (Nobel Lecture, December 11, 1945). NobelPrize.org.
bio-evo-05-c1.quote: The time may come when penicillin can be bought by anyone in the shops. Then there is the danger that the ignorant man may easily underdose himself and by exposing his microbes to non-lethal quantities of the drug make them resistant.
bio-evo-05-c1.claim: Alexander Fleming, who discovered penicillin, warned in his 1945 Nobel lecture that misuse would breed resistant bacteria.

bio-evo-05-c1.text: Antimicrobial Resistance Collaborators (2022). Global burden of bacterial antimicrobial resistance in 2019: a systematic analysis. The Lancet.
bio-evo-05-c1.quote: One pathogen–drug combination, meticillin-resistant S aureus, caused more than 100 000 deaths attributable to AMR in 2019
bio-evo-05-c1.claim: He was right: MRSA (Staphylococcus aureus resistant to methicillin) now causes more than 100,000 deaths a year.

bio-evo-05-c2.text: Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institutet (2022). Press release: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2022. NobelPrize.org.
bio-evo-05-c2.quote: Research provided evidence that the anatomically modern human, Homo sapiens, first appeared in Africa approximately 300,000 years ago
bio-evo-05-c2.claim: Homo sapiens emerged ~300,000 years ago in Africa; modern human behaviour appeared ~70,000–100,000 years ago.

bio-evo-05-c2.text: Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institutet (2022). Press release: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2022. NobelPrize.org.
bio-evo-05-c2.quote: This relationship was first seen in populations in Melanesia and other parts of South East Asia, where individuals carry up to 6% Denisova DNA.
bio-evo-05-c2.claim: Non-African humans carry ~1–4% Neanderthal DNA; Melanesians carry up to 6% Denisovan DNA.

bio-evo-05-c3.text: Weidong Feng, Yinan Li, Paschalis Kratsios (2022). Emerging Roles for Hox Proteins in the Last Steps of Neuronal Development in Worms, Flies, and Mice. Frontiers in Neuroscience.
bio-evo-05-c3.quote: Hox genes were first discovered in Drosophila during the 20th century; genetic experiments identified mutants with dramatic phenotypes caused by homeotic transformations (e.g., legs instead of antennae in Antp mutants, duplication of thoracic segments in Ubx mutants)
bio-evo-05-c3.claim: Mutations in Hox genes can produce dramatic changes: Antennapedia mutant flies grow legs where antennae should be.

bio-evo-06-c1.text: Georgia Tsagkogeorga, Michael R. McGowen, Kalina T. J. Davies, et al (2015). A phylogenomic analysis of the role and timing of molecular adaptation in the aquatic transition of cetartiodactyl mammals. Royal Society Open Science.
bio-evo-06-c1.quote: Molecular evidence has revealed that the closest living relatives of the cetaceans are the two extant members of the family Hippopotamidae: the common and pygmy hippopotamus
bio-evo-06-c1.claim: For example, hippos are closer to whales than to pigs; mushrooms are closer to animals than to plants; placental mammals diversified after the dinosaur extinction.

bio-evo-06-c2.text: Simon Ho (2008). The Molecular Clock and Estimating Species Divergence. Nature Education (Scitable).
bio-evo-06-c2.quote: Subsequent research has shown that Kimura's assumption of a strict molecular clock is too simplistic, because rates of molecular evolution can vary significantly among organisms.
bio-evo-06-c2.claim: Different genes tick at different rates, and rates can vary across lineages.

bio-evo-07-c1.text: Béla Suki (2012). The Major Transitions of Life from a Network Perspective. Frontiers in Physiology.
bio-evo-07-c1.quote: In an influential work, Maynard Smith and Szathmáry (1995) argued that the majority of the increase in complexity is not gradual, but it is associated with a few so-called major transitions along the way of the evolution of life.
bio-evo-07-c1.claim: Maynard Smith and Szathmáry (1995) catalogued the major transitions in evolution: events where new levels of biological organization arose.

bio-evo-07-c2.text: Michael W. Gray (2017). Lynn Margulis and the endosymbiont hypothesis: 50 years later. Molecular Biology of the Cell.
bio-evo-07-c2.quote: The 1967 article “On the Origin of Mitosing Cells” in the Journal of Theoretical Biology by Lynn Margulis (then Lynn Sagan) is widely regarded as stimulating renewed interest in the long-dormant endosymbiont hypothesis of organelle origins.
bio-evo-07-c2.claim: Lynn Margulis pushed endosymbiotic theory in the 1960s, against initial resistance.

bio-evo-07-c3.text: C. Athena Aktipis, Amy M. Boddy, Gunther Jansen, et al (2015). Cancer across the tree of life: cooperation and cheating in multicellularity. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B.
bio-evo-07-c3.quote: Complex multicellularity has evolved independently at least seven times (once in Metazoa, once each in ascomycete and basidiomycete fungi, once in embryophytes, once in chlorophytes and at least once in both the rhodophytes and heterokontophytes)
bio-evo-07-c3.claim: Multicellularity has evolved many times: animals, plants, fungi, and several lineages of algae.

bio-evo-08-c1.text: Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institutet (1995). Press release: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 1995. NobelPrize.org.
bio-evo-08-c1.quote: He found that the genes were arranged in the same order on the chromosomes as the body segments they controlled.
bio-evo-08-c1.claim: Hox genes pattern body segments in flies, fish, mice, and us: in roughly the same order on the chromosome.

bio-evo-08-c1.text: Walter J. Gehring (2011). Chance and Necessity in Eye Evolution. Genome Biology and Evolution.
bio-evo-08-c1.quote: Pax6 was identified as a master control gene for eye morphogenesis and found to be involved in eye development of all bilaterian animals
bio-evo-08-c1.claim: Pax6 induces eye development in flies and mice.

bio-evo-08-c2.text: Kevin N. Laland, Tobias Uller, Marcus W. Feldman, et al (2015). The extended evolutionary synthesis: its structure, assumptions and predictions. Proceedings of the Royal Society B.
bio-evo-08-c2.quote: Developmental, or phenotypic, plasticity is the capacity of an organism to change its phenotype in response to the environment.
bio-evo-08-c2.claim: An organism's response to environment (plasticity) can shape its evolution.

bio-evo-08-c3.text: Richard G. Klein (2023). Profile of Svante Pääbo: 2022 Nobel laureate in physiology or medicine. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
bio-evo-08-c3.quote: Svante Pääbo, a Swedish geneticist who directs the Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology in Leipzig, Germany, was awarded the 2022 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for pioneering the extraction and analysis of DNA from ancient bones, above all those of the Neanderthals.
bio-evo-08-c3.claim: Ancient DNA: techniques pioneered by Pääbo (Nobel 2022) recovered Neanderthal genomes and showed Homo sapiens interbred with Neanderthals and Denisovans.

bio-evo-08-c3.text: Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institutet (2022). Press release: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2022. NobelPrize.org.
bio-evo-08-c3.quote: In modern day humans with European or Asian descent, approximately 1-4% of the genome originates from the Neanderthals

bio-evo-08-c3.text: John S. Favate, Kyle S. Skalenko, Eric Chiles, et al (2023). Linking genotypic and phenotypic changes in the E. coli long-term evolution experiment using metabolomics. eLife.
bio-evo-08-c3.quote: Begun in 1988, the LTEE populations have evolved for more than 75,000 generations, making it the longest running experiment of its kind.
bio-evo-08-c3.claim: Experimental evolution: Lenski's E. coli have evolved in flasks for >75,000 generations, accumulating beneficial mutations.

bio-evo-03-c2.text: Meredith M. Doellman, Gregory J. Ragland, Glen R. Hood, et al (2018). Genomic Differentiation during Speciation-with-Gene-Flow: Comparing Geographic and Host-Related Variation in Divergent Life History Adaptation in Rhagoletis pomonella. Genes.
bio-evo-03-c2.quote: The recent shift of R. pomonella from its ancestral host downy hawthorn (Crataegus mollis) to introduced domesticated apple (Malus domestica) in the mid-1800s is an example of ecological divergence-with-gene-flow, hypothesized to also represent speciation in action
bio-evo-03-c2.claim: Apple maggot flies (Rhagoletis pomonella) began colonising introduced apple trees in the 1800s and are diverging from hawthorn-feeding relatives despite occupying the same geographic area, driven by different host preferences.
